## Writing

Full text is hosted on this site. Each piece was originally published on X; the X link is kept at the bottom of each article.

- [The Next Software Industry Is Humans Writing Rules for Agents](https://www.dinoilievski.com/writing/the-next-software-industry-is-humans-writing-rules-for-agents.html) (Oct 14, 2026): Agents that write their own skills do worse than agents with none; human-written skills jump performance 16.6 points. As agents become the layer over the software stack, every layer is an incomplete contract — and unlike other layers, agents have no law, norms, or culture to fill the gaps. The new software industry is humans writing rules, harnesses, and duties for their agents.
- [Your Agent's Duties Shouldn't Belong to Its Vendor](https://www.dinoilievski.com/writing/your-agents-duties-shouldnt-belong-to-its-vendor.html) (Oct 10, 2026): The law treats an AI agent as a tool, so liability lands on whoever deployed it — yet its duties are whatever its vendor configured. Agency law solved the principal-agent problem for humans with limits of authority, records, escalation, and liability. Those duties should be written once by the principal, enforced from outside the agent, and carried everywhere it acts.
